## One Thing

They clearly understand what a run and trace are, and how to see them in an agent observability platform (LangSmith in this case)

## Outcomes

Define agent observability terms: run, trace, and tracing
Identify when and when not to use tracing diagnostics
Be intimately familiar with the tracing UI in LangSmith
- Identify in LangSmith a run and trace
- Identify in LangSmith every type of run: LLM, Retriever, Tool, Chain, Prompt, and Parser
- Identify in LangSmith input, output, and metadata

## Prep

Make sure you have traces to share in the Slack for them to open and navigate. Between the traces, all these components should be found:

![](../Assets/Images/types_of_runs_langsmith_small.png)

## Notes

The outcomes are met by going through the slides and activities.

They should be set up in LangSmith, but they don't need to be for the activities. This should be expected they can do on their own at this point.

Simple outline:
- What and why LangSmith: usefullness in industry, is it sticking around, when to use it
- What and why Trace/run
- Show how to navigate trace
- They navigate and explore trace
- Continue primer/practice, which is setting up their own account and running own traces

Traces can be shared, so prepare some traces for them to navigate and identify the parts of a trace.
